verification.expected_output: Learner can demonstrate the concept and explain it.

execution_timeline: Research what employers expect for planning a job-ready Go portfolio at the target experience level.
Review current portfolio or skill level against those expectations and identify gaps.
Create or improve the artifact addressing the largest gap first.
Get feedback from a peer, mentor, or community review.
Incorporate feedback and iterate until the artifact meets the job-ready bar.

failure_modes.cause: The learner treats preparation as an infinite loop instead of a finite gate.
failure_modes.fix: Set a deadline, ship the artifact, and start applying. Iterate based on real interview feedback.

performance_implications: Focusing on planning a job-ready Go portfolio yields diminishing returns after the job-ready threshold — prioritize breadth over depth at this stage.

Audit current portfolio and identify the biggest gap related to planning a job-ready Go portfolio.
Plan the artifact: scope, timeline, technologies, and success criteria.
Build the artifact with tests, documentation, and a README.
Submit for peer review, incorporate feedback, and publish.

Portfolio strategy exists because the final step from learner to professional Go engineer requires packaging competence into a format that employers can evaluate: a portfolio, interview performance, and professional network.
